text: On an exact-referee build task, one strong agent reached the org's hidden scores for half the money and half the minutes. Cold starts and the architect's hop cost the org; most waves were one module's problem.
The org built a layered compiler shaped like its org chart, with eleven times the tests, that compiles about 40% slower. Structure leaks into the product.

When the problem fits one context, one agent found the cross-cutting wins (parallel load, direct linking, faster tokens) in its first round; three org designs all landed near 0.62 at 1.2-3.7x its cost.

One strong agent built a near-gcc optimiser in one session but shipped two wrong-code bugs every check it could run passed; the hidden W1-W5 gate caught them. The org's merged compiler passed the hidden gate. The org's advantage is independent checking, not breadth.
Give fewer workers longer rounds: 45-minute rounds were too short for a back-end redesign and four warm workers burned the budget four times faster than one agent.
Put a held-out correctness check inside the referee: the merge check lacked the hidden-style W1-W5 coverage that caught V's miscompiles.
A judge can be wrong: 126 of 3,624 reference files had been written with the same flaw; an org worker (w-measure) found it, and the referee then falsely reverted that worker's merge.
